slot.brief: Identify which aldehyde undergoes Cannizzaro reaction and why (no α-hydrogen); could include a mild computation of the mole ratio of alcohol to acid formed.

stem: Among propanal, butanal, 2-methylpropanal and benzaldehyde, which undergoes the Cannizzaro reaction because it has no α-hydrogen? On complete reaction of $0.40$ mol in concentrated aqueous NaOH, followed by acidification, what amounts of alcohol and acid are formed?
options: Propanal; $0.20$ mol propan-1-ol and $0.20$ mol propanoic acid
Benzaldehyde; $0.40$ mol benzyl alcohol and $0.40$ mol benzoic acid
Benzaldehyde; $0.20$ mol benzyl alcohol and $0.20$ mol benzoic acid

verdicts.working: Only benzaldehyde has no α-hydrogen. Cannizzaro stoichiometry is 2 mol aldehyde → 1 mol alcohol + 1 mol carboxylate; acidification gives 0.20 mol each from 0.40 mol benzaldehyde.

working:
$2\,\text{C}_6\text{H}_5\text{CHO}+\text{OH}^-\rightarrow\text{C}_6\text{H}_5\text{CH}_2\text{OH}+\text{C}_6\text{H}_5\text{COO}^-$
$0.40/2=0.20$ mol each of alcohol and acid after acidification.
Benzaldehyde has no α-hydrogen.

Independent check: Only benzaldehyde has no α-hydrogen. Cannizzaro stoichiometry is 2 mol aldehyde → 1 mol alcohol + 1 mol carboxylate; acidification gives 0.20 mol each from 0.40 mol benzaldehyde.
solution:
Benzaldehyde has no α-hydrogen, so it undergoes the Cannizzaro reaction.
$$2\,\mathrm{C_6H_5CHO}+\mathrm{OH^-}\rightarrow\mathrm{C_6H_5CH_2OH}+\mathrm{C_6H_5COO^-}$$
Thus, $0.40$ mol benzaldehyde forms $0.20$ mol benzyl alcohol and, after acidification, $0.20$ mol benzoic acid.
